sentences.text: 6. It appears that the accused persons, i.e., the appellants before us, prayed for discharge before the Trial Court.
The in- laws of respondent No.2 came to be discharged whereas the Trial Court proceeded to frame charge against the husband for the offences enumerated above.

7. In the aforesaid context, two Revision Applications came to be filed in the Sessions Court; one by the original complainant against the order discharging the in-laws and another by the husband against the order declining to discharge.
The Sessions Court remanded the matter to the Trial Court and, accordingly, both  4 the Revision Applications came to be disposed of.
As against the order passed by the Sessions Court, the accused persons went to the High Court.
The High Court proceeded to pass the impugned order.
8. In such circumstances, referred to above, the appellants are before this Court.
9. We heard Mr. Sarad Kumar Singhania, the learned counsel appearing for the appellants/original accused persons and Mr. Adab Singh Kapoor, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
We have also heard Mr. S.D. Sanjay, the learned Additional Solicitor General for the respondent-State.
10. We take notice of the following relevant aspects of the matter:
The marriage between Pradeep Kumar and Kanchan Premi was solemnized on 19.07.2010 in the State of Himachal Pradesh.

sentences.text: On 29.09.2010, the couple left for the United States.
On 06.12.2011, a child was born in the wedlock.
In the month of February, 2013, a complaint came to be lodged before the Delhi Police by the mother of Kanchan Premi.
It appears from the materials on record that the couple got divorced by mutual consent in the USA on 06.11.2013.

The Decree of Divorce was passed by the Court of State of Missouri,
USA.
The alimony and child support amounting to $75,600 was fixed by the U.S. Court.
It is not in dispute that this amount of $75,600 has been paid by the husband to his wife and the custody of the child is also with the father.
11. There is one further development we should take notice of.

On 16.09.2015, Kanchan Premi (respondent No.2 herein) got re-  5 married in the United States to one US citizen and on 24.12.2018,
the husband also got re-married.
12. In the aforesaid factual background, we are of the view that no useful purpose would now be served in allowing the criminal proceedings to continue further.
We also take notice of the fact that the wife never ever came to India to prosecute her husband and the in-laws.
We have been informed that the father-in-law, namely,
Chint Ram, has passed away.
13. In such circumstances, referred to above, the impugned order passed by the High Court is set aside.
The criminal proceeding arising from the FIR No.147/2013, pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, is hereby quashed.
14. Both the appeals stand allowed in the above terms.
